### open-contracting/cardinal-rs
- URL: https://github.com/open-contracting/cardinal-rs
- Exact commit / revision: `7441f76529fbdefbc5666b4ce0d5b844e7f1056c`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: Active MIT Rust engine that calculates procurement red flags and statistical indicators directly from Open Contracting Data Standard compiled releases. The inspected implementation covers concrete indicators including short submission periods, single-bid tenders, identical bid prices, late winning bids, disqualification patterns, supplier heterogeneity and heavily discounted bids, with OCID/buyer/procuring-entity/tenderer grouping plus configurable exclusions and statistical-fence metadata.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It converts normalized procurement history into deterministic competition-friction evidence instead of another opportunity search surface. The project is small by attention but deep enough to become an analytic layer over heterogeneous SLED/international OCDS feeds.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon capture/BD teams, procurement-intelligence vendors, public procurement oversight/integrity teams, SLED consultants and market researchers.
- Painful problem: Historical procurement feeds answer what was published or awarded but not where bidding patterns look unusually concentrated, thin, disqualification-heavy or price-anomalous; reproducing defensible indicator semantics independently is domain-heavy and easy to get wrong.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price agency or SLED competition-friction diagnostic: normalize several years of tenders, calculate reviewable red flags, link every flag back to source releases, and deliver a capture/market-risk packet. Sell recurring monitoring only after source completeness is proven.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 2-4+ months saved on OCDS indicator semantics, grouping/statistical logic, configuration, edge-case handling and fixture design.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact current revision; repository tree with indicator implementations/fixtures/benchmarks; indicator documentation; `src/indicators/r018.rs` implements single-bid detection only for configured procurement methods by reading `tender.numberOfTenderers`, rather than relying on README claims alone.
- License / rights: MIT for repository code. Upstream procurement datasets retain source/publisher terms.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT, subject to source-data rights and validation on each publisher. Indicators are signals for review, not findings of fraud or illegality.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Only modest GitHub attention and a standards-tooling name hide a ready procurement-risk analytics engine; its commercial value appears only after combining it with evidence-preserving acquisition/normalization.
- Value score: **28/30** — A4, B4, C5, D5, E5, F5. Fastest revenue is an analytic diagnostic; ceiling is somewhat below a full capture platform but domain compression and rights are excellent.
- Combination opportunities: SLED collectors -> immutable raw/hash snapshots -> `open-contracting/kingfisher-process` lifecycle normalization -> Cardinal indicators -> CaptureBrief evidence packet. Pair with Bluetail-style ownership relationships only as separate evidence, never as misconduct inference.
- Next action: Run Cardinal against 2-3 rights-clean SLED/OCDS publishers and score indicator reproducibility, missing-field behavior, source traceability and false-positive review burden before adding any customer-facing risk label.

### miroslav-jokovic/fuel-guard — regulatory truth-release pipeline
- URL: https://github.com/miroslav-jokovic/fuel-guard
- Exact commit / revision: `768b541e0c5dd3171b1cbc57ef782384e09caa22`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong
- What it contains: MIT application whose undernoticed `hazmat-data` package implements an evidence-grade regulated-data release process for 49 CFR hazardous-materials tables: point-in-time eCFR Title 49 XML, independent GovInfo annual CFR XML, frozen real-source parser fixtures, exhaustive cross-source diff/reconciliation, Federal Register/eCFR currency checks, SHA-256 release checksums and a provisional/fail-closed production gate.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The strongest asset for this hunt is the acceptance architecture, not the fuel UI. A regulatory dataset cannot graduate to production merely because parsing succeeded: unexplained source disagreements block release, effective-pending rules are surfaced, a named human attestation is part of the release path, and clearing remains provisional until the triangulation gate passes.
- Likely buyer / user: GovCon/compliance SaaS teams, regulated-logistics software, eligibility engines, audit products and any product making deterministic decisions from changing federal rules.
- Painful problem: Compliance products often ingest one official endpoint and silently turn parser/source drift or lag between publications into confident current-law conclusions.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Reuse the release discipline to build a paid CaptureBrief regulatory-truth layer: versioned FAR/DFARS/SBA reference releases with two-source or independent-publication cross-checks where available, currentness monitoring, checksums and explicit provisional/unresolved states. Separately, the native hazmat package could support implementation services in regulated logistics.
- Build-time / data advantage: Roughly 2-4 months of source-triangulation, parser-fixture, diff, currentness, attestation and fail-closed release design; more importantly it supplies a rare production-safety pattern.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact current revision; `packages/hazmat-data/RELEASING.md` documents eCFR versioner point-in-time Title 49 XML as Source A, GovInfo annual CFR XML as Source B, frozen parser fixtures, exhaustive row diff/reconciliation, Federal Register plus `latest_amended_on` currency checks, release SHA-256, named attestation and forced provisional state unless the cross-check is clean. The documented HMT/placard/segregation verification counts are treated as repository evidence, not independently re-certified legal truth.
- License / rights: MIT for repository code. Government-source publications and any embedded/reference artifacts retain their own provenance/rights and must be version-pinned.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT for the software/pattern; independently establish rights/currentness for each source dataset.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Zero-star application branding hides a sophisticated regulated-data publication discipline in a subpackage rather than marketing it as compliance infrastructure.
- Value score: **27/30** — A4, B4, C5, D5, E5, F4. Rights for code are clear; underlying regulatory artifacts still need source-specific treatment.
- Combination opportunities: Apply its release gate to `GSA/GSA-Acquisition-FAR`, eCFR/agency-deviation feeds and SBA size-standard references: authoritative snapshot -> parser fixture -> independent cross-check/correction review -> currency watcher -> checksum/attestation -> only then deterministic eligibility/compliance output.
- Next action: Implement a small FAR/SBA reference-release prototype with `verified/provisional/stale/conflict` states and prove that a stale or disagreeing source cannot yield a customer-facing definitive result.

### criticaljuncture/ecfr-xml-corrections
- URL: https://github.com/criticaljuncture/ecfr-xml-corrections
- Exact commit / revision: `39925f3ef81012dda8eae4f97bbf020a25286851`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch / clean-room only
- What it contains: Zero-star active corpus of eCFR XML correction patches with per-patch metadata for description, structural/transcription/amendment-date class, OFR approval state, Federal Register document/reference and date-bounded applicability. It also documents tooling for diagnosing malformed/reversed amendment-date ranges.
- Rare or undernoticed value: This is a compact real-world corpus of failure modes that regulatory parsers usually discover only in production. The explicit `approved` versus `needs-approval` state and date-scoped applicability are especially useful requirements for point-in-time law ingestion.
- Likely buyer / user: Legal/regulatory data vendors, GovCon compliance products, eCFR parsers and research platforms.
- Painful problem: Treating eCFR XML as perfectly clean can corrupt point-in-time text or amendment chronology without obvious errors.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Clean-room the observed anomaly classes into a regulatory-ingestion regression suite and source-quality monitor; sell the higher-value compliance/evidence product that fails visibly when currentness or correction status is unresolved.
- Build-time / data advantage: Several weeks to 1-2 months of obscure eCFR edge-case discovery and temporal-correction test design.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision and README; patch metadata model; `structural`, `transcription` and `amendment-date` tags; `approved`/`needs-approval` status; patch start/end applicability; Federal Register/reference fields and amendment-date diagnostic description.
- License / rights: No repository-wide license established at the inspected revision.
- Reuse classification: Inspect/learn/clean-room only unless permission is established. Independently re-derive any correction handling from official/public source evidence before implementation.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Tiny correction repository with no marketing layer, but it exposes exactly the pathological temporal/XML cases that authoritative regulatory products must survive.
- Value score: **20/30** — A3, B3, C3, D5, E5, F1. Rare evidence and completeness are strong; no-license status sharply limits direct reuse.
- Combination opportunities: LexBuild/Axiom/eCFR ingestion + this clean-room anomaly taxonomy + Fuel Guard-style multi-source release gating + CaptureBrief FAR/deviation evidence.
- Next action: Build independent regression fixtures for malformed amendment dates, date-bounded corrections and approval-state ambiguity using official eCFR/Federal Register evidence; do not copy patch content.
